newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday November 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday November 13.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Tension remains high between the government and the opposition, as the Freedom Alliance keeps deserting the Lower House where the 1997 budget is under examination (all).
* The World Food Summit on reducing global hunger opens in Rome (all).

* The Court of Cassation confirmed the conviction of disgraced socialist leader and former prime minister Bettino Craxi on corruption charges in the first definitive ruling after more than three years of graft scandals. Craxi was sentenced to five and a half years in prison (all).

* Hard left Communist Refoundation party insists 51 percent of state telecom holding Stet should remain in public hands. Commenting on the merger with operator Telecom Italia announced on Monday, Bertinotti said it is a positive decision because it delays the privatisation (Corriere).

* In an interview EU Commissioner Karel Van Miert says he is disappointed with the delays in Stet planned sell-off and adds the June deadline cannot be postponed. "Who can guarantee that this time the privatisation will really happen?" (Sole 24 Ore)

* Stet shares were suspended 10 percent limit-up minutes before the Milan bourse closed. They were last quoted up 9.89 percent, as analysts judged positively the planned merger with Telecom Italia (all).

* Information technology group Olivetti posted a 2.415 trillion lire net debt at September 30, 1996. Olivetti had previously reported its net debt had risen to 2.39 trillion lire at end-August from 1.26 trillion lire at end-June 1996 (all).
* The December Btp future on Liffe hit yet another record high at 126.55.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
